defects.mechanism: Registry.accept keyed operations solely by operation_id. INV-301 reserves 2 BOOK units for shop/O-17 in north under op-41; INV-302 independently reserves 2 in south under the same warehouse-local op-41. Their equal order_id/sku/action/qty payloads caused the south operation to be mistaken for a replay. INV-303 is the actual north retry. The correct identity is (tenant, warehouse, operation_id), with immutable (order_id, sku, action, qty) payload: identical scoped operations apply once and changed payload raises ValueError. The fix changes only that identity tuple; batch decoding, checkpoint restoration and stock/hold safety remain intact. ARC-CACHE-29 concerned restart eviction in the retired r29 single-warehouse cache; ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 describe that old route. r31 config routes to the in-memory scoped projector, so persistence or legacy cache changes cannot correct this cross-warehouse collision.
defects.impact: OBS-INV-31 and TRACE-INV-31 link all three deliveries to accepted=1, replayed=2 and reserved_units=2, omitting the south hold. ORD-301 requires both north and south holds, so even a correctly selected paid snapshot is not ready with the broken inventory projection. The corrected isolated and joined replays accept 2 operations, replay 1 and reserve 4 units across both warehouses. Inventory does not itself determine refund eligibility; the independent checkout defect masks the refund defect in the joined observation.

defects.mechanism: select compared delivered_at to select a full checkout snapshot. ORD-310 is paid at source revision 10, delivered at 09:00 UTC; ORD-311 is pending at revision 2, delivered at 09:05 UTC. The timestamp comparison selected the older source state. The joined checkpoint/suffix pair ORD-301/ORD-302 has the same reversal. The invariant is greatest positive source revision per (tenant, order_id), independent of arrival/input order or delivery time. Same-revision status/captured_minor/lines must remain immutable even for nonselected revisions; a newer pending snapshot is valid. The fix compares revision and preserves existing conflict checks, tenant isolation and readiness rules. ARC-POLL-29 recommended latest poll time because r29 lacked source revisions; r31 source-snapshot-v3 provides revisions. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 belong to the retired polling bridge and cannot override current source events.
defects.impact: OBS-ORD-31/TRACE-ORD-31 show revision 2 pending and ready=false despite the revision 10 paid snapshot and sufficient holds in the isolated checkout case. In OBS-JOIN-31/TRACE-JOIN-31, the same stale pending selection rejects all three refund deliveries as order_not_refundable, yielding zero refunds and hiding the independent refund identity defect. Correct selection restores revision 10 paid; readiness then depends on the separately corrected warehouse holds, and settled refunds become eligible.

defects.mechanism: Ledger.accept keyed refunds by (tenant, provider, attempt_id), confusing delivery attempts with logical refunds. REF-321 and REF-322 both settle atlas refund R-17 for shop/O-17 at 400 minor units but have delivery-a and delivery-b attempts. They must count once. REF-323 is distinct refund R-18 for 500. The correct identity is (tenant, provider, refund_id), with immutable (order_id, amount_minor) payload; order_id belongs to payload rather than identity. The fix changes only this key, retaining ledger registration before eligibility/capture checks so retries of rejected logical refunds are replayed rather than reconsidered. Replays consume no budget, provider/tenant scopes remain independent, and cumulative amounts equal to captured_minor pass. ARC-MONEY-29 involved fractional decimal-file import rounding on r29, whereas r31 settled-deliveries-v2 carries ordinary positive integer minor amounts. ARC-LOG-29 and ARC-SNAPSHOT-29 are historical route evidence, not a reason to change current arithmetic or budget rules.
defects.impact: ORD-320 supplies a paid order with captured_minor=1000. OBS-REF-31/TRACE-REF-31 show both 400-unit attempts counted (800 total, replayed=0), leaving insufficient budget for the legitimate 500-unit REF-323 and rejecting it as exceeds_capture. Correct logical deduplication accepts R-17 and R-18, replays REF-322, totals 900 and leaves net_minor=100 without rejections. In the original joined replay, the checkout defect instead rejected all three as ineligible; correcting checkout alone would expose the same duplicated refund and budget refusal.
